src/app/export/export.controller.ts: filter building is passed to this.apiService.buildFiltersFromQueryParams(...) and the export itself to this.exportService.export({...}), so the work happens in the application layer.
src/app/export/export.controller.ts: the user id and settings come from the injected REQUEST (this.request.user), which is a request-context concern.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The export controller does only presentation-layer work. It defines the HTTP route with @Controller and @Get, applies authentication and permission guards and the request/response interceptors, and binds the query parameters. Its only data handling is turning the comma-separated query strings into arrays with split(','), which is transport-level input parsing. It passes the filter parameters to ApiService.buildFiltersFromQueryParams and hands the actual export to ExportService.export, along with the user id and settings taken from the request. It contains no persistence logic, no business rules and no domain calculations. The @prisma/client import is only used as a type cast. Import direction is out of scope for this check.
